You are building the **Website Builder (Wix-style) Phase-1 MVP** for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres + a serial job worker). The full design is in docs/PLAN-WEBSITE-BUILDER.md — READ IT FIRST, it is authoritative on architecture and reuse.

## MVP scope (build exactly this)
Customer picks a template → edits text/images in a GrapesJS editor in the portal → clicks Publish → a `SITE_PUBLISH` job renders the editor document to a static HTML/CSS bundle and writes it atomically into `/var/www/<domain>`, reusing the existing nginx vhost + auto-SSL machinery. Publish target for the MVP is a `*.nxeon` subdomain. Drafts saved in Postgres. 3–5 templates, a core block set (GrapesJS preset-webpage provides blocks). Mobile breakpoints (GrapesJS device manager). NO custom domains, NO forms backend, NO e-commerce yet.

## Schema is ALREADY in the DB and Prisma client is generated — do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma
Models available now: `Site` (id,userId,name,slug,websiteId?,status[DRAFT|PUBLISHING|PUBLISHED|FAILED],templateKey?,publishedAt?,error?), `SitePage` (siteId,path,title,seoDesc?,sortOrder), `SiteVersion` (siteId,document Json,label?,isDraft,publishedAt?), `SiteAsset` (siteId,path,filename,mimeType,sizeBytes). JobType enum already has `SITE_PUBLISH` and `SITE_UNPUBLISH`.

## GrapesJS is already installed centrally
`grapesjs@0.23.3` and `grapesjs-preset-webpage@1.0.3` are in node_modules. Import them in a CLIENT component only (`"use client"`), load GrapesJS in a useEffect (it touches `window`/DOM). Use its HTML+CSS export (`editor.getHtml()` + `editor.getCss()`) as the published output — static, no runtime. Store the editor project data (`editor.getProjectData()`) as the `SiteVersion.document` JSON for reloading the draft.

## Reuse (per the plan — do not reinvent)
- Publish pipeline models on `worker/websites.ts` (`nginxVhost()`, `/var/www/<domain>`, `nginx -t` gate, exit-code checks). READ that file.
- File write over SSH/SFTP: reuse `lib/ssh-exec.ts` + `lib/sftp.ts` (the same helpers websites.ts uses).
- A `Site` PUBLISHES INTO a `Website` row (reuse it for the nginx/SSL binding) — do not duplicate vhost/cert concerns.
- **Publish MUST be atomic**: render to a temp dir, then swap (rsync-with-delete into a staging path then move, or symlink swap). A failed publish must never leave a half-written live site. This is the one genuinely fiddly bit — get exit-code checks + the `nginx -t` gate right, exactly as websites.ts does.
- Gate behind an `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH` env flag mirroring `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` (worker/websites.ts:~39): in SANDBOX/staging (NXEON_SANDBOX) the worker SIMULATES the publish (mark PUBLISHED without touching real infra). Ships to prod dormant.

## Files you OWN (create/edit only these)
- `app/dashboard/sites/**` — list page + editor page
- `components/customer/site-builder/**` — the GrapesJS editor wrapper (client), template picker, publish/draft controls
- `lib/actions-sites.ts` — server actions: create site, save draft, publish (enqueue SITE_PUBLISH), unpublish, list, delete, rename. `"use server"`.
- `lib/site-render.ts` — PURE, testable: editor document → final static HTML/CSS string(s) per page. No IO.
- `lib/site-templates.ts` — the 3–5 starter templates (data + their initial GrapesJS documents)
- `worker/site-publish.ts` — the `sitePublish` and `siteUnpublish` handler functions (export them), modeled on worker/websites.ts
- `test/site-render.test.ts`, `test/site-actions-guards.test.ts` (or similar) — tests
- The CUSTOMER portal nav: add a "Sites" entry. Find the customer sidebar nav definition (the plan says components/portal/Shell.tsx — locate the actual nav list). You may edit that ONE nav file to add the entry. If it turns out to be shared with admin nav (lib/admin-groups.ts), do NOT edit it — instead put the exact entry in your final report for central wiring.

## Files you must NOT touch (I wire these centrally — put instructions in your report)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` (frozen)
- `worker/index.ts` — I will add `SITE_PUBLISH: sitePublish, SITE_UNPUBLISH: siteUnpublish` to the handlers map and the import. In your report, give me the EXACT import line and the two handler-map lines.
- `lib/admin-groups.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts` (admin-only; not your concern)

## Platform rules (non-negotiable — learned the hard way here)
- `"use server"` files: EVERY export is a public network endpoint. Auth + ownership checks go INSIDE each function. Every action must `requireUser()` (find the helper, e.g. lib/auth) and ownership-check the site by `userId: user.id`. A user must never act on another user's Site.
- Honesty invariant: a Site is only `PUBLISHED` when the publish REALLY succeeded (bundle written, nginx reloaded green). On any failure set status FAILED + `error`, never fake success. Mirror how worker/websites.ts checks exit codes.
- Every test must actually bite. For source-shape tripwires use `stripCommentsAndStrings`/`stripComments` from `test/_source-tools.ts` (never a raw grep — it hits incident comments). Assert every lib/actions-sites.ts export authenticates and ownership-checks.
- Tests run with `npm test` (node:test). tsc must be clean for your files: `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- Slug → subdomain must be sanitized (lowercase, `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing dash) and unique.
- Do NOT run: `prisma db push`/`migrate` (schema already applied), `next build` in place, `git commit`, deploy, or `systemctl`. I integrate centrally.
- Prisma client is generated. If you add nothing to schema you don't need to regenerate.

## Deliver
Self-contained, typechecking code + tests. Final report: (1) the exact worker/index.ts import + handler-map lines I must add; (2) which nav file you edited (or the entry for me to add); (3) any new env var (ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH) and where it's read; (4) test count; (5) anything you simulated vs really wired. Report is data for me, not a user message.

1	# Build plan — Website Builder
2	
3	*Status: PROPOSAL. Documents only. No code, schema, or infrastructure has been built. The owner decides go/no-go from this.*
4	
5	*Written 2026-07-27 to the same honesty standard as `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: concrete file references, real tradeoffs, reuse over greenfield.*
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Executive summary
10	
11	A Wix-style drag-and-drop site builder: a customer picks a template, edits text and images in the browser, clicks Publish, and has a live SSL site on a real domain minutes later. **Unlike the cloud phone, this needs no new hardware and no new architecture** — it lands almost entirely on machinery Nxeon already runs. We already turn edited content into a live, SSL'd, domain-bound site: that is exactly what the control panel's Websites tab does today (`worker/websites.ts`, `lib/actions-websites.ts`, the `Website` model at `prisma/schema.prisma:1145`, automatic DNS via `lib/cloudflare-point.ts`, and the certificate sweep in `worker/ssl.ts`). The builder is a new *front door* — a browser editor and a publish pipeline — bolted onto that existing back door. The right technical bet is **adopt an open-source editor and publish static files**, not build an editor or run a per-site runtime. The MVP is: pick a template, edit text/images, publish to a `*.nxeon` subdomain with auto-SSL. The main blocker is not engineering risk — it is **content and support**: templates good enough that non-technical users get a nice result, and the support load that a non-technical audience brings. The honest verdict: feasible and well-matched to the platform; the hard part is design and support, not infrastructure.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Why this fits Nxeon (the thing to lean into)
16	
17	Everything after "click Publish" already exists and is battle-tested in production:
18	
19	- **The publish target is `/var/www/<domain>` served by nginx** — the exact layout `worker/websites.ts` already creates and manages (`nginxVhost()` generates the server block; `nginx -t` gates every reload; exit codes are genuinely checked — `worker/websites.ts:131`).
20	- **SSL is automatic** via `SSL_ISSUE` + the 30-minute `sslSweep` reconciliation in `worker/ssl.ts` — the same path that keeps every customer site's certificate alive today.
21	- **Domain binding** already works two ways: registration/DNS through `lib/registrar.ts` (name.com) and automatic A-record pointing through `lib/cloudflare-point.ts` (`proxied: false` so HTTP-01 validates — `lib/actions-websites.ts:164`).
22	- **Bandwidth of published sites is already metered** (`lib/bandwidth.ts`), and **the worker job model** (`JobType` enum at `prisma/schema.prisma:35`, `handlers` map at `worker/index.ts:944`) is the exact place a `SITE_PUBLISH` job belongs, right beside `WEBSITE_CREATE`.
23	
24	So the builder reuses the entire hosting/SSL/domain/billing/worker stack and adds one editor and one publish job. That is why it is far more achievable than the cloud phone.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Editor approach — adopt, don't build
29	
30	Building a drag-and-drop editor from scratch is a multi-quarter project and a trap. Adopt a mature open-source foundation and spend our effort on templates and the publish pipeline instead.
31	
32	| Foundation | Model | Output | License | Fit |
33	|---|---|---|---|---|
34	| **GrapesJS** | Framework-agnostic drag-drop editor with a built-in webpage preset | **Exports plain HTML + CSS** | BSD-3 | **Best fit for the MVP** — static HTML/CSS drops straight into `/var/www/<domain>`; no runtime; matches our nginx static-hosting exactly |
35	| **Puck** (`@measured/puck`) | React visual editor over a **JSON document**; renders React components (blocks) | JSON → rendered React (SSG or runtime) | MIT | Best if we want a structured block/JSON model and are willing to render React; cleaner data model, but adds a render step |
36	| **Craft.js** | A React *framework for building* page editors — you build the editor UI | Whatever you build | MIT | More control, much more work; only if the above two constrain us |
37	| Gutenberg-style block model | Heavy WordPress-lineage block system | — | GPL | Overkill; ignore |
38	| **Build our own** | — | — | — | No. Reinventing a solved, hard problem |
39	
40	**Recommendation:** **GrapesJS for the MVP** because its HTML/CSS export lands with zero runtime on the hosting we already run. Keep **Puck** as the option if, in Phase 3, we want a richer structured block model and are ready to introduce a render step. The block/section library and templates are *our* work either way — that is where the product's quality lives.
41	
42	**Templates and blocks.** A starter set of professionally-designed templates (landing page, restaurant, portfolio, small-business, one-pager) and a block/section library (hero, features, gallery, pricing, contact, footer). This is design labour, not engineering, and it is ongoing. **Mobile-responsive editing** (desktop/tablet/mobile breakpoint switching) is table stakes — GrapesJS and Puck both support device breakpoints; the responsibility is authoring templates that actually hold up at each width.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Hosting + publish pipeline
47	
48	**Static export, not a rendered runtime.** The MVP publishes a static bundle (HTML/CSS/JS/assets) into a docRoot served by nginx. No per-site process, no runtime to crash, no per-tenant memory cost, minimal attack surface, and it slots into the existing hosting with no changes to how sites are served. A rendered/dynamic runtime (server-side CMS, live forms backend) is a deliberate later phase, not the starting point.
49	
50	**The pipeline, reusing what exists:**
51	
52	```
53	Editor (browser, in app/dashboard)
54	      │  save  → Site/SitePage JSON in Postgres (draft)
55	      ▼
56	[ Publish ] → enqueue Job  SITE_PUBLISH        ← new JobType, beside WEBSITE_CREATE
57	      ▼
58	worker/site-publish.ts (new, modelled on worker/websites.ts)
59	      │  1. render the site JSON → static HTML/CSS/assets
60	      │  2. write the bundle into /var/www/<domain> over SSH/SFTP
61	      │        (reuse lib/ssh-exec.ts + lib/sftp.ts — same helpers websites.ts uses)
62	      │  3. ensure the nginx vhost exists (reuse nginxVhost() / WEBSITE_CREATE)
63	      │  4. reload nginx  (nginx -t gate, exactly as today)
64	      ▼
65	worker/ssl.ts  →  SSL_ISSUE + sslSweep  (unchanged, automatic cert)
66	lib/cloudflare-point.ts / lib/registrar.ts  →  domain bound (unchanged)
67	```
68	
69	**Two hosting destinations, phased:**
70	
71	1. **Shared "builder" host (MVP).** Customers who don't own a VPS publish to a `*.nxeon` subdomain on a single shared builder VM. This is one small VM (well within our ~291 G NVMe free per `pvesm status`) and gives a zero-friction "publish in one click" first experience. A `Website` row per published site binds it to nginx; SSL is automatic on the subdomain.
72	2. **Customer's own VPS + custom domain (Phase 2).** Publish straight into a `Website`/docRoot on the customer's existing server — the builder becomes another producer of the same `Website` rows the control panel already manages, on their own domain with their own cert.
73	
74	**Publish must be atomic.** Write the new bundle to a temp dir and swap the docRoot symlink (or rsync-with-delete into a staging path then move), so a failed publish never leaves a half-written live site. `worker/websites.ts` already checks exit codes and gates on `nginx -t`; the publish job must add the same rigour to the file write. Call this out to whoever builds it — it is the one genuinely fiddly bit.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Data model (additive only)
79	
80	New models, none touching existing tables — same additive style as `EmailPlan`/`GamePlan` sitting beside `Plan`:
81	
82	| Model | Purpose | Notes |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| `Site` | One website a customer is building | `userId`, `name`, optional `websiteId` (the `Website` row it publishes into once live), publish state |
85	| `SitePage` | A page within a site | `siteId`, `path` (`/`, `/about`), `title`, SEO fields |
86	| `SiteVersion` | An immutable snapshot of the editor document | `siteId`, `document` (JSON — the GrapesJS/Puck doc), `createdAt`; a `draft` pointer and a `publishedVersionId` pointer give drafts + rollback for free |
87	| `SiteAsset` | Uploaded media (images) | `siteId`, storage path/URL, size — feeds storage/bandwidth accounting |
88	
89	Publish state lives as `Site.status` (`DRAFT` / `PUBLISHING` / `PUBLISHED` / `FAILED`) mirroring the string-status convention the `Website` model already uses (`prisma/schema.prisma:1145`). Reuse the existing `Website` row for the actual nginx/SSL binding rather than duplicating that concern — a `Site` *publishes into* a `Website`.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## How it reuses existing systems
94	
95	- **Billing** — a builder plan tier / entitlement, priced in integer cents through the existing checkout, renewal, and dunning machinery (same pattern as `EmailPlan`, `prisma/schema.prisma:710`). No new billing code. Could also be a feature flag on existing hosting plans.
96	- **Provisioning / publish worker** — `SITE_PUBLISH` (+ `SITE_UNPUBLISH`) added to `JobType` (`prisma/schema.prisma:35`) and the `handlers` map (`worker/index.ts:944`), beside `WEBSITE_CREATE`. Serial worker, retries, reaping — all free.
97	- **Domain + SSL binding** — `lib/registrar.ts`, `lib/cloudflare-point.ts`, and `worker/ssl.ts`'s `SSL_ISSUE`/`sslSweep`, entirely unchanged.
98	- **Hosting layer** — `worker/websites.ts`'s `nginxVhost()`, the `/var/www/<domain>` convention, and `lib/ssh-exec.ts` / `lib/sftp.ts` for the file write.
99	- **Portal** — a new "Sites" section under `app/dashboard` using `components/portal/Shell.tsx`; the editor is client-side JS hosted inside the existing Next.js app. No new service.
100	- **The gate pattern** — an `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH`-style flag mirroring `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` (`worker/websites.ts:39`), so it ships to prod dormant and SANDBOX/staging simulate the publish.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## MVP definition
105	
106	**Pick a template → edit text and images inline → publish to a `*.nxeon` subdomain with automatic SSL.** One shared builder host, a handful of templates, a limited block set, static export, drafts saved in Postgres. No custom domains yet, no forms backend, no e-commerce. This is genuinely shippable on current hardware and reuses the entire publish/SSL/domain stack.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## Phased milestones
111	
112	**Phase 1 — MVP.** GrapesJS embedded in `app/dashboard`; `Site`/`SitePage`/`SiteVersion` models; `SITE_PUBLISH` job → static bundle → shared builder host → auto-SSL subdomain; 3–5 templates; core block library; mobile breakpoints; drafts. Behind the publish gate flag.
113	
114	**Phase 2 — Custom domains + versioning polish.** Publish into the customer's own VPS `Website`/docRoot on their own domain (reuse `lib/registrar.ts` + `worker/ssl.ts`); draft/publish/rollback UX on `SiteVersion`; a media/asset library with storage accounting; more templates and blocks; SEO fields per page.
115	
116	**Phase 3 — Full editor + dynamic bits.** Richer block editor (possibly the Puck/JSON model); **contact forms wired to the existing mailer** (`lib/mailer.ts` — form submission → email, no new infra); analytics; optional structured content. A rendered runtime only if a real feature (e.g. a CMS collection) demands it.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## Infrastructure and cost
121	
122	**Low, and mostly already paid for.** The editor is client-side JS inside the existing Next.js portal — no new service, no GPU, no new host. Costs to watch, none alarming:
123	
124	- **Storage** — site JSON in Postgres is tiny; uploaded media is the real consumer. Put media on the NVMe pool (291 G free, `pvesm status`) for the builder host, or the 4 TB HDD pool for cold assets; add a per-plan storage quota via `SiteAsset` accounting.
125	- **Bandwidth** — published static sites are served from nginx and already metered by `lib/bandwidth.ts`. Static sites are cheap to serve; a viral customer site is the only spike risk, bounded by plan limits.
126	- **Shared builder host** — one small VM, trivially within current headroom.
127	
128	The one platform constraint to remember: **the worker is strictly serial** (`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, "Architecture at a glance"). A publish is a short job, so this is fine — but a slow publish still queues behind a 24-minute migration like everything else. Keep the publish job fast (render + rsync, seconds) so it never becomes the thing blocking the queue.
129	
130	---
131	
132	## Risks
133

model WalletTransaction {
  stripeSessionId       String?  @unique

  id                    String   @id @default(cuid())

model Website {

## Report — Website Builder Phase-1 MVP

### 1. worker/index.ts — exact lines to add (I did NOT touch this file)

### 2. Nav file edited

### 3. New env vars (all read only in `worker/site-publish.ts`)
- `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH` — gate mirroring `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL`. `REAL = !SANDBOX && process.env.ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH === "1"`. Ships dormant.
- `SITE_BUILDER_BASE_DOMAIN` — base domain for the `*.<base>` subdomains (default `"nxeon.site"`). Also read by the two page files for display. **Set this to your real builder base domain.**
- `SITE_BUILDER_SERVER_ID` — the `Server` row id of the shared builder host to SSH into. Required when `REAL`; a real publish throws a clear error if unset.

### 4. Test count
**18 tests, all passing** (verified under the real `tsx --test` harness): `test/site-render.test.ts` (9 — pure renderer: slug sanitization, file mapping, HTML escaping, self-contained output, empty/missing-home refusal, collision detection, wire-shape validation) and `test/site-actions-guards.test.ts` (9 — structural tripwires via `stripCommentsAndStrings`: every action authenticates, `ownedSite` proves `userId` ownership, all mutators route through it, actions never import the SSH layer, worker gates on `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH`+`SANDBOX`, refuses fake success with flag off in both handlers, renders-before-write + exit-code + `nginx -t` checks, atomic release-dir-then-`mv` swap). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (0 errors).

### 5. Really wired vs simulated
- **Really wired:** the full render → SSH write → atomic swap → `nginx -t` gate → `reloadNginx` (with post-reload `is-active` check) → `verifyServing` probe pipeline, reusing `sshServer`/`nginxVhost`/`ensureNginx`/`reloadNginx` from `worker/websites.ts` and `withServerSsh`/`exec`/`execInput`/`assertDomain`/`assertPath`/`shellQuote` from `lib/ssh-exec.ts`. A `Site` publishes INTO a `Website` row (`ensureBuilderWebsite`, retry-safe against `@@unique([serverId,domain])`) bound to the builder server, so the existing SSL sweep picks up the subdomain unchanged. Atomicity: bundle is built in full into `/var/www/<domain>.rel-<jobId>`, then swapped in with `mv` (a rename); a failure before the swap leaves the live docRoot untouched; both critical `mv`s are exit-code checked.
- **Simulated (by design):** in `NXEON_SANDBOX` the worker marks the site `PUBLISHED` and writes a published `SiteVersion` snapshot without any SSH — notifications say so explicitly. On a prod box with the flag OFF (`!REAL && !SANDBOX`) both handlers **throw** rather than fake success (honesty guard mirroring `websiteCreate`). A `Site` reaches `PUBLISHED` only after the real work verifiably succeeds.
